messages:
elena: Hey runtime team — prepping the webinar and launch post. We need a very small, well-documented handoff of bench artifacts for the slides and press claims. Key asks: heatmap (coldstart vs steady), 50/95/99 latency percentiles, tokens/sec and cost-per-1k-tokens for fp16 + int8/quantized variants, and a short warmup profile (what sequence lengths and requests to run). Can we get a smoke rerun and a reproducible command/trace that marketing can attach?

matt: Quick clarifying q: which model+variant should we run? also target batch size / concurrency? and do you want tail percentiles measured per-request or per-token?

elena: Model: redwood/3b-compat-v1 (prod-ish config). Compare fp16 and int8-qs8 where available. Batch size: 1 and 8. Concurrency: 1 and 16 (to show coldstart vs throughput). Percentiles: per-request end-to-end. Sequence lengths: short (32 tokens), medium (192), long (1024).

sophie: Also add: we might claim a cost delta in the talk (not headline), so please include the raw token counts + billing units used so we can compute $/1k tokens. If there are caveats (warmup artifacts, KV cache effects), call them out. :pray:

andy: We can run a lightweight sweep tomorrow morning. Plan: run 2x warmup iterations, then 200 samples per cell (batch/concurrency/seqlen). We'll capture 50/95/99, CPU/GPU utilization, and per-token latency breakdowns. Can whoever owns the sample payloads drop them here?

elena: Dropped sample set link: https://gist.example.com/redwood/webinar-samples (contains 10 prompty variations per seqlen). Use the prompt labeled "webinar-clean" — no safety edgecases.

matt: Thanks. One more: do you want absolute numbers or normalized (relative to hosted baseline)? marketing wants an "apples-to-apples" comparison.

elena: Both please — raw metrics + normalized chart against hosted-fp16 (same model). Add 95% CI where possible. If quantized runs show instability on long context, call that out explicitly.

andy: Understood. We'll also produce a minimal reproduce block like below that we can attach.

andy: ```
# reproduce smoke (example)
curl -sS -X POST https://runtime.internal.redwood/api/v1/generate
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $RUNTIME_TOKEN'
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json'
  -d '{"model":"redwood/3b-compat-v1","input":"<sample>","max_tokens":64,"batch":1}'
```

runtime-bot: Job queued: run_id=job-2026-5599-01, ETA ~2h. See /internal/bench/runs/job-2026-5599-01 for logs.

matt: If we hit any weird nondeterminism on int8, we'll capture stderr and the exact commit+kernel versions. I'll try to have a small README with the kernel selection and environment (CUDA, cuDNN, driver versions).

sophie: Timeline: marketing needs the artifact bundle (CSV + small explainer + one slide image) by Thu 18:00 PT. If you can't make that, call it out now so we can adjust content.

andy: Ack — aiming for Wed EOD run and Thu morning artifacts. If any runs flop, we'll surface minimal notes and a suggested conservative claim.

elena: Thanks all. Please @matt and @andy on updates. For the slide we want a single heatmap (coldstart x seqlen) and a two-column chart (throughput vs $/1k tokens). Keep it simple.

matt: On it. I'll post run summary + attach CSV once the job completes.

runtime-bot: Job completed: run_id=job-2026-5599-01, artifacts: /internal/bench/artifacts/job-2026-5599-01.zip (contains CSV, traces, env.txt)
